blocks.text: Why use Notion for customer onboarding managers on Mac

Most onboarding managers feel the weight of information asymmetry. Sales teams pass over a deal, but the context often stays in emails or disconnected spreadsheets. Notion allows you to build a single source of truth. You can create a database for your clients and then add properties for status, priority, and assigned CSM. On a Mac, the desktop app is fast and keeps your workspace separate from your browser tabs. This helps you focus when you need to update project statuses or review client documentation.

Start by creating a master database for your clients. Use the `/database` command to add a table. Add properties for 'Status', 'Onboarding Date', and 'Account Manager'. A clean database is the foundation of a good workflow. You can then use the 'Filter' button to create views for 'Active Onboarding', 'Pending Handoff', and 'Completed'. This ensures you only see what you need to work on right now.
Using Lazur to manage your Notion workspace

When you are deep in a client page, you do not want to hunt for settings. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about your screen. You can ask 'Where do I add a new property here?' or 'How do I filter this view?' Lazur points at the menu items on your Mac screen. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on your client data. It is a faster way to learn the interface without leaving your current task.
Practical Notion tips for onboarding managers

items: Create a template for your kickoff meetings. Use the `/template` command inside your database to pre-fill the page with your agenda, action items, and client requirements.
Use callouts for important client notes. Type `/callout` to highlight critical information like account risks or special requests.
Link your client documents. Use the `@` symbol to mention other pages or databases to keep everything connected.
Keep your sidebar clean. Use nested pages to group client folders by quarter or region.
Use the 'Status' property to track progress. You can customize the labels to match your specific onboarding stages, such as 'Discovery', 'Technical Setup', and 'User Training'.

blocks.text: Handling the sales to CS handoff

The handoff is where most information is lost. Create a standard handoff form in Notion. Require fields like 'Client Goals', 'Key Stakeholders', and 'Pain Points'. When a sales rep finishes a deal, they fill out this form. This gives you all the context you need before your first call. It removes the need for long email threads and ensures you start the relationship on the right foot.

Do not overcomplicate your database. Start with basic properties. You can always add more as your team grows. Avoid creating too many separate databases. Keep related information together so you can use linked views to show data in different ways. Do not rely on manual updates for everything. Use formulas to calculate days since the last contact or to highlight overdue tasks.

faq.question: Can I use Notion for client-facing portals?
faq.answer: Yes. You can publish a Notion page to the web and share the link with your clients. This is a great way to show them their onboarding progress.

faq.question: How do I speed up my workflow in Notion on Mac?
faq.answer: Learn the keyboard shortcuts. Press ⇧ + ? to see the full list. Using slash commands like /table or /callout will save you significant time every day.

faq.question: What if my Notion database is too slow?
faq.answer: If you have thousands of entries, try to use filtered views to limit what the app loads at once. Also, make sure you are using the desktop app on a supported version of macOS.
